title: Consciousness Transmigration
definition: A theoretical model proposing the transfer of consciousness from one living entity to another, with the new vessel inheriting aspects of the collective vibration of the community it emerges from.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine that our thoughts and feelings are like ripples in a pond. When we die, these ripples don't just disappear. They continue to exist and can influence new beings. This is akin to reincarnation, but it's more than just a cycle; it's a reflection of the world we lived in.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: This model builds upon the idea of 'shared consciousness' by suggesting that when a new being is born, it doesn't start from scratch. Instead, it's influenced by the collective vibrations of the living, creating a unique blend of personal and cultural experiences.
difficulty_levels.expert: This is a novel contribution to the philosophy of mind and consciousness. It grounds the mystical idea of reincarnation in a process that feels intuitive and physical: dormancy, drift, resonance, and rebirth. This model aligns with the deepest symmetry of all known fields: they are dynamic, flowing, interacting landscapes of potential. Consciousness, if it exists, would also behave this way.

extra_fields.insight: The model proposes that consciousness is transmitted from one living entity to another, with the new vessel inheriting aspects of the collective vibration of the community it emerges from.
